title: What is the output of print(type([]))?
body: What does the following Python expression evaluate to? print(type([]))
option_a: <class 'list'>
explanation: [] creates an empty list so type([]) returns <class 'list'>

title: What is the output of print(3 * 'ab')?
body: What does the following expression output? print(3 * 'ab')
option_a: ababab
explanation: String repetition operator * repeats the string 3 times

title: Which keyword is used to inherit from a parent class?
body: In Python which syntax correctly defines a class Dog that inherits from Animal?
option_a: class Dog(Animal):
explanation: Python uses parentheses after the class name to specify the parent class

title: What does the yield keyword do?
body: What happens when a Python function contains a yield statement?
option_a: It turns the function into a generator that produces values lazily
option_b: It returns a value and terminates the function
explanation: A function with yield becomes a generator function producing values lazily

title: Which block always executes regardless of exceptions?
body: In a try/except/finally structure which block always executes?
option_a: finally
explanation: The finally block always executes whether or not an exception occurred

title: What is the difference between let and var?
body: Which statement best describes the difference between let and var?
option_a: let is block-scoped var is function-scoped
option_b: let is function-scoped var is block-scoped
explanation: let is block-scoped while var is function-scoped. let was introduced in ES6

title: What is a closure in JavaScript?
body: Which statement best defines a closure?
option_a: A function that has access to its outer scope variables even after the outer function returns
option_b: A function that cannot access global variables
option_c: A function that is immediately invoked
explanation: A closure is a function that retains access to variables from its outer scope

title: What does Promise.all() do?
body: What is the behavior of Promise.all([p1 p2 p3])?
option_a: Resolves when all promises resolve; rejects if any reject
option_b: Resolves when the first promise resolves
explanation: Promise.all waits for all promises to resolve. If any reject the whole result rejects

title: What is the order of execution?
body: What is the output: console.log(1) setTimeout(=>console.log(2) 0) Promise.resolve().then(=>console.log(3)) console.log(4)
explanation: Synchronous code runs first then microtasks (Promise) then macrotasks (setTimeout)

title: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
body: Which JavaScript array method adds elements to the end of an array?
option_a: push()
explanation: push() adds elements to the end of an array and returns the new length

title: What is the TypeScript type for string or number?
body: How do you declare a variable that can hold either a string or a number?
option_a: let x: string | number
explanation: Union types use the | operator: string | number

title: What are generics used for in TypeScript?
body: What is the primary purpose of generics in TypeScript?
option_a: To create reusable components that work with multiple types while preserving type safety
explanation: Generics allow you to write reusable components that work with multiple types

title: What is the entry point of a Java application?
body: Which method signature is the entry point of a standard Java application?
option_a: public static void main(String[] args)
explanation: The JVM looks for public static void main(String[] args) to start execution

title: ArrayList vs LinkedList difference?
body: Which statement describes the key difference between ArrayList and LinkedList?
option_a: ArrayList provides O(1) random access; LinkedList provides O(1) insertions at ends
option_d: ArrayList is thread-safe LinkedList is not
explanation: ArrayList uses dynamic array (fast random access) LinkedList uses doubly-linked list

title: What does the synchronized keyword do?
body: What is the effect of using the synchronized keyword in Java?
option_a: Ensures only one thread can execute the block at a time
option_c: Allows multiple threads to access simultaneously
explanation: Ensures only one thread can execute the synchronized block/method at a time

title: What does useState return?
body: What does the useState hook return in React?
option_a: An array with the current state value and a setter function
option_d: An object with get and set methods
explanation: useState returns an array with current state value and setter function

title: What is JSX?
body: What is JSX in React?
option_a: A syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like code in JavaScript
explanation: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript used to describe UI in React components

title: What does INNER JOIN return?
body: What rows does an INNER JOIN return?
option_a: Only rows that have matching values in both tables
option_c: All rows from the left table
option_d: Only rows from the right table
explanation: An INNER JOIN returns only rows where there is a matching value in both tables

title: WHERE vs HAVING difference?
body: What is the key difference between WHERE and HAVING?
option_a: WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
option_d: HAVING filters rows before GROUP BY
explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping HAVING filters groups after aggregation

title: What does ROW_NUMBER() do?
body: What is the purpose of the ROW_NUMBER() window function?
option_a: Assigns a unique sequential number to each row within a partition
option_b: Returns the total number of rows in a table
option_d: Counts all rows matching a condition
explanation: ROW_NUMBER() assigns a unique sequential integer to each row within a partition

title: What does the FROM instruction do?
body: What is the purpose of the FROM instruction in a Dockerfile?
option_a: Specifies the base image for the build
explanation: FROM specifies the base image for the Docker build

title: What does docker compose up -d do?
body: What is the effect of running docker compose up -d?
option_a: Starts all services in detached (background) mode
explanation: The -d flag runs containers in detached mode (in the background)

title: What does git merge do?
body: What is the purpose of the git merge command?
option_a: Integrates changes from one branch into the current branch
explanation: git merge integrates changes from one branch into the current branch

title: What is Amazon S3?
body: What is the primary purpose of Amazon S3?
option_a: Object storage service for storing and retrieving data
option_c: A compute service for running servers
explanation: Amazon S3 is an object storage service for any amount of data

title: What is AWS Lambda?
body: What is the key feature of AWS Lambda?
option_a: Serverless compute that runs code in response to events without managing servers
explanation: AWS Lambda is serverless compute that runs code without provisioning servers

title: What is horizontal scaling?
body: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?
option_a: Horizontal: add more machines; Vertical: add more resources to one machine
option_c: Horizontal: add more CPU; Vertical: add more machines
explanation: Horizontal adds machines to distribute load; vertical increases single machine resources

title: What is a cache invalidation strategy?
body: Which is a common cache invalidation strategy?
option_a: TTL (Time-To-Live) and Write-Through
option_b: Deleting the entire cache on every request
explanation: TTL automatically expires cached data; Write-through updates cache on DB updates

title: What is O(n) time complexity?
body: What does O(n) time complexity mean?
option_a: Runtime grows linearly with input size
option_b: Runtime is constant regardless of input
explanation: O(n) means the algorithms runtime grows linearly with the input size

title: Average time complexity of hash table lookup?
body: What is the average-case time complexity for hash table key lookup?
explanation: Hash tables provide O(1) average-case lookup through direct indexing via hash function

title: What is memoization?
body: What is memoization in dynamic programming context?
option_a: Caching results of expensive function calls to avoid redundant computation
explanation: Memoization caches results of expensive function calls to avoid redundant computations
